trustPages.label: About
trustPages.title: About PalCalculator | Fan-Made Palworld Calculator Tools
trustPages.description: Learn what PalCalculator does, why it exists, how its fan-made Palworld calculator data is reviewed, and where to report corrections safely.
trustPages.keywords: PalCalculator about, Palworld calculator about, fan-made Palworld tools
intro: PalCalculator is an unofficial fan-made calculator and guide site for Palworld players who want clearer planning tools before spending in-game resources.

The site focuses on practical questions: which parent pair should I check, can I route from the Pals I already own, how should I read a caveated IV or stat estimate, and what passive goals should I plan separately from a breeding route?

sections.heading: Why PalCalculator exists
paragraphs: Palworld breeding and stat planning can become confusing quickly. A simple target can involve parent availability, route length, passive inheritance, IV ranges, data freshness, and patch timing.
PalCalculator brings those workflows into one browser-based hub, pointing players toward direct parent-pair lookup, owned-Pal route planning, IV estimation, expected stat bands, or passive planning.

sections.heading: What the site can help with
paragraphs: Use PalCalculator when you want to check a parent pair, search possible parents for a target Pal, compare a route from owned Pals, understand why a result is unavailable, estimate broad IV ranges, preview stat bands, or organize passive goals before choosing breeders.
The tools are planning aids. Results depend on the selected data version, supported formulas, public source quality, patch timing, and user inputs.

sections.heading: Independent fan-made status
paragraphs: PalCalculator is independent and fan-made. References to Palworld, Pal names, game mechanics, patches, or related terms are used so players can identify the game content they are planning around.
PalCalculator is not affiliated with, endorsed by, sponsored by, or approved by Pocketpair or the Palworld team.

sections.heading: How the site treats data and caveats
paragraphs: The site uses public game-data references, selected formula assumptions, and visible data-version notes. Some areas are intentionally marked as unsupported when the current build does not have enough reviewed information.
Current examples include caveats around verified special-combo override coverage, passive inheritance probabilities, server-side save uploads, and full IV exactness with every possible modifier.

sections.heading: Who maintains PalCalculator
paragraphs: PalCalculator is maintained at the site level by the PalCalculator maintainer/team. The site can remain brand-level while still giving users a clear correction path.

For data corrections, privacy questions, or broken-page reports, use the Contact page. Reports should include the Pal name, route or calculator used, game version, current result, expected result, and a source or reproduction note.

faqs.question: Is PalCalculator official?
faqs.answer: No. PalCalculator is an unofficial fan-made Palworld calculator and guide site.

faqs.question: What is PalCalculator for?
faqs.answer: It helps players plan parent-pair checks, owned-Pal routes, IV/stat estimates, passive goals, and data-version caveats before spending in-game resources.

faqs.question: Who maintains the site?
faqs.answer: The site is maintained under the PalCalculator maintainer/team name while offering a public correction path through Contact.

faqs.question: Does PalCalculator replace in-game verification?
faqs.answer: No. Use results as planning guidance tied to the current dataset, then verify in game when patch timing or resource cost matters.

trustPages.label: Contact
trustPages.title: Contact PalCalculator | Corrections, Privacy & Data Reports
trustPages.description: Contact PalCalculator for Palworld data corrections, privacy questions, broken pages, or calculator caveats without sending private save files.
trustPages.keywords: PalCalculator contact, Palworld calculator corrections, PalCalculator data report
intro: Use this page to report data corrections, broken links, calculator caveats, privacy questions, or copy that seems unclear.
Please do not send passwords, tokens, private account details, save files, full Palbox exports, or personal identifiers.

sections.heading: Public contact path
paragraphs: For the current recovery release, start from the public correction workflow on Data Sources at /data-sources/#corrections and include only details needed to reproduce the issue.
If the owner later approves a dedicated email alias, issue tracker, form, or social contact profile, this page should be updated before the next AdSense review request.

sections.heading: What to include in a data correction
paragraphs: Include the Pal name, calculator page or guide URL, game version or patch context, current PalCalculator result, expected result, source link if available, and steps to reproduce the issue.

Helpful example: I searched Anubis on /breeding-calculator/, selected target-to-parent mode, and the current data version showed an unavailable state. Here is the source link and patch context for review.

sections.heading: What not to send
paragraphs: Do not send account passwords, API keys, cookies, save files, payment details, personal identifiers, or screenshots that expose private information.
If a report depends on your owned-Pal list, summarize the relevant Pals in plain text instead of uploading a full save or private inventory file.

sections.heading: What happens after a report
paragraphs: Reports should be reviewed against the current data sources, current app behavior, and editorial policy.
Some reports may not become immediate site changes, especially when the data is patch-sensitive, conflicting, or outside the current supported domains.

sections.heading: Privacy and advertising questions
paragraphs: For privacy questions, include the page URL, browser behavior you noticed, and whether the issue concerns localStorage, share URLs, analytics, or advertising scripts.

For advertising concerns, include the page URL and a short description. Ads may support site maintenance, but ad placement should not change calculator output or require an account, payment, or login gate.

faqs.question: Do I need an account to report a correction?
faqs.answer: No PalCalculator account is required. Use the public correction workflow described on this page and Data Sources.

faqs.question: Should I send my save file?
faqs.answer: No. Do not send save files or private identifiers. Summarize only the Pal names, page, result, and source details needed for review.

faqs.question: What makes a correction report useful?
faqs.answer: A useful report includes the Pal name, page URL, game version, current result, expected result, source link, and reproduction notes.

faqs.question: Can I report ad or privacy concerns here?
faqs.answer: Yes. Include the page URL and a short description of the issue without sending private account, token, or payment details.

trustPages.label: Editorial Policy
trustPages.title: Editorial and Data Review Policy | PalCalculator
trustPages.description: Read how PalCalculator reviews fan-made Palworld calculator copy, data caveats, source conflicts, unsupported states, and correction reports.
trustPages.keywords: PalCalculator editorial policy, Palworld data review policy, calculator caveats
intro: PalCalculator should be useful even before a user interacts with JavaScript.
The policy is simple: do not invent results, do not hide uncertainty, and do not turn a player workflow into a claim that the current data cannot support.

sections.heading: Editorial goals
paragraphs: Every indexable page should help a real Palworld player complete a planning task. A page should explain what the tool does, what inputs matter, how to read outputs, what limits apply, and where to go next.
Pages should not exist only to repeat route links or capture keywords.

sections.heading: Data and example rules
paragraphs: Exact parent pairs, route steps, special-combo labels, passive probability claims, and narrow IV interpretations should only be published when generated from current app data and reviewed for caveats.
When current data is incomplete, the correct editorial choice is to explain the unsupported state.

sections.heading: How source conflicts are handled
paragraphs: Public data sources can disagree because of patch timing, naming, aliases, special-combo assumptions, or parsing gaps.
A correction can lead to a data update, a clearer limitation, a changed guide example, or a decision to keep a result unavailable until the current dataset supports it.

sections.heading: Guide page selection
paragraphs: New guide pages should be chosen because they answer a distinct search or player workflow.
Thin pages, duplicated templates, and placeholder pages should not be added to the sitemap.

sections.heading: Language rules
paragraphs: Use practical language such as estimate, range, planning guidance, current dataset, reviewed example, unsupported state, and data-version caveat.
Avoid positive claims that imply rights-holder status, total coverage, instant freshness, certain outcomes, or probability support the app does not provide.

sections.heading: Review cadence and visible dates
paragraphs: Trust pages and data-source notes should include a visible last-reviewed or last-updated date.
After major Palworld updates, review the data-version page, core calculator pages, and thin guide pages before publishing more search pages.

sections.heading: Corrections workflow
paragraphs: Correction reports should include page URL, Pal name, calculator mode, current result, expected result, source link, game version, and reproduction notes.
Reports should not require save files, account tokens, or private identifiers.

faqs.question: Does PalCalculator publish invented routes?
faqs.answer: No. Exact routes should be generated from current app data and reviewed, or the page should explain the unsupported state instead.

faqs.question: Why do pages use caveats so often?
faqs.answer: Caveats help players understand patch timing, unsupported formulas, source conflicts, and data-version limits before spending resources.

faqs.question: Can a thin guide still be useful?
faqs.answer: Only if it answers a distinct task with original explanation, examples, FAQs, and links.

faqs.question: How are corrections reviewed?
faqs.answer: Reports are compared against current sources, app behavior, and data limitations before changing copy or data.

trustPages.title: Advertising Disclosure | PalCalculator
trustPages.description: Learn how PalCalculator may use ads or sponsor disclosures, how ads support maintenance, and why ads do not affect calculator results or access.
trustPages.keywords: PalCalculator advertising disclosure, Palworld calculator ads, fan site disclosure
intro: PalCalculator may display advertising, including Google AdSense, to help support maintenance of the fan-made calculator and guide site.
No account, payment, subscription, or checkout is required to use the core calculators described here.

sections.heading: How advertising may appear
paragraphs: Advertising may appear as standard page ads or clearly labeled sponsor/support messages if the owner later approves them.
If Google AdSense is used, Google may use cookies or similar technologies for ad delivery, measurement, fraud prevention, and personalization controls.

sections.heading: Ads do not change calculator output
paragraphs: Calculator results, caveats, source notes, and guide recommendations should not change because of an ad, advertiser, sponsor, or potential affiliate relationship.
If PalCalculator ever adds sponsored links, affiliate links, or paid placements, those items should be clearly labeled near the relevant link or section.

sections.heading: No paywall requirement
paragraphs: The site remains a public browser-based calculator hub. Users should not need to create an account, pay, upload a save file, or provide private details to use core planning workflows.
A gentle support message is acceptable when it does not pressure users, hide calculator output, or make trust pages sound like a checkout funnel.

sections.heading: Reporting ad concerns
paragraphs: If an ad appears broken, misleading, intrusive, or too close to a calculator result, users can report the page URL and a short description through Contact.
Do not ask users to send private account details, tokens, payment information, or save files when reporting an ad issue.

faqs.question: Does advertising affect calculator results?
faqs.answer: No. Ads should not affect calculator output, caveats, source notes, or guide copy.

faqs.question: Do users need to pay to use PalCalculator?
faqs.answer: No account, checkout, or payment is required for the core calculator workflows.

faqs.question: Does PalCalculator use Google AdSense?
faqs.answer: The site may display Google AdSense ads. Privacy copy explains cookies, measurement, and personalization controls.

faqs.question: How should sponsor or affiliate links be handled?
faqs.answer: Any sponsor, affiliate, or paid placement should be clearly labeled near the link or section where it appears.

blocks.heading: What PalCalculator helps you decide
body: PalCalculator helps with five common Palworld planning jobs: checking parent pairs, planning a route from Pals you already own, estimating IV ranges, comparing expected stat bands, and organizing passive-skill goals before you choose breeders.

Start from the question you can answer right now. If you know two parents, use the Breeding Calculator. If you know the target Pal but not the path, use Route. If you already have a candidate Pal, use IV or Stats. If your plan is about traits, use Passives before returning to breeding or route planning.

table.Why: Searches for a bounded path from owned Pals to the target.

Captures passive goals without claiming inheritance outcomes.

blocks.heading: Beginner example: I want Anubis but only own Penking and Bushi
body: First, search Anubis in the Breeding Calculator to understand target-parent options for the current dataset. Next, open the Route Calculator with Anubis as the target and Penking, Bushi as owned Pals.
After the target route is practical, move to Passives if you care about work, combat, movement, or breeder traits. Use IV and Stats only after you have candidates to evaluate.

blocks.heading: Use the site safely
body: PalCalculator is an unofficial fan-made site. Treat results as planning guidance tied to the current dataset, not as a rights-holder source or a promise about every future patch.
Check data-version notes before following a long route. Recheck after major updates, when another guide disagrees, or when a result depends on special-combo behavior.

blocks.heading: Data and privacy at a glance
body: Owned-Pal route helpers remain browser-local unless a future reviewed feature clearly says otherwise. No account, server-side Palbox upload, or payment is required for the core calculator workflows described here.
For source categories, unsupported domains, corrections, privacy details, terms, and advertising transparency, use the Trust & data links in the footer.

faqs.question: Which Palworld calculator should I use first?
faqs.answer: Use Breeding for direct parent-pair checks, Route for owned-Pal paths, IV for hidden stat estimates, Stats for expected stat bands, and Passives for trait planning.

faqs.question: Is PalCalculator fan-made?
faqs.answer: Yes. PalCalculator is an unofficial fan-made site with visible data-version and caveat notes.

faqs.question: Are owned Pals uploaded to a server?
faqs.answer: The current owned-Pal helper is browser-local localStorage only, with no account, upload, or backend sync.

blocks.heading: What this calculator does
blocks.body: Use the Breeding Calculator for direct parent-child questions. Pair to Child is for two known parents. Target to Parents is for the Pal you want.

blocks.heading: Pair to Child vs Target to Parents
blocks.body: Pair to Child answers: if I breed these two Pals, what child does the current dataset return? Target to Parents answers: which parent-pair options should I review for this target?

blocks.heading: Example: Penking + Bushi
blocks.body: Use Penking + Bushi as an editable pair example to show how a direct lookup works. The explanatory copy focuses on reading the result, combo type, rule label, and caveats.

blocks.heading: Example: Anubis target lookup
blocks.body: Search Anubis as the target when the question is which parents may produce Anubis in the selected dataset.

blocks.heading: Unavailable or special-combo states
blocks.body: If a Pal, pair, alias, or special-combo state is unsupported, show that state directly. Do not fill missing data with an unreviewed combo from another chart.

blocks.heading: Common mistakes
items: Using Pair to Child when the real question is target planning.
Treating one parent pair as a full route.
Assuming passive inheritance is solved by the same combo.
Following old screenshots without checking data version.

faqs.question: When should I use Pair to Child?
faqs.answer: Use it when you already know two parents and want to check the child result in the current dataset.

faqs.question: When should I use Target to Parents?
faqs.answer: Use it when you know the Pal you want and need possible parent pairs to review.

faqs.question: Does a parent pair decide passive skills?
faqs.answer: No. Use passive planning separately because inheritance can involve RNG and current data limits.

blocks.heading: What a route calculator adds beyond a combo list
blocks.body: A combo list answers one parent-child relationship. The Route Calculator answers whether your current Pals can connect to the target within a practical generation limit.

blocks.heading: Inputs that shape the route
blocks.body: The key inputs are target Pal, owned Pals, and max generations. Owned-Pal state is browser-local localStorage only in the current product.

blocks.heading: How to read a route
blocks.body: A useful route result explains generation count, ordered steps, the route tree, missing Pals, alternatives, and caveats.

blocks.heading: Example: route to Anubis from Penking + Bushi
blocks.body: Use the existing editable demo with target Anubis, owned Pals Penking and Bushi, and max generations 3.

blocks.heading: When no route appears
blocks.body: No route can mean strict constraints, too few owned Pals, unsupported data, spelling mismatch, special-combo limits, or patch differences.

blocks.heading: Compare practical routes
items: Fewer generations are simpler, but missing parents may matter more.
A route using owned Pals can be easier than a shorter route that requires rare parents.
Passive goals may change which parent candidates are worth keeping.

faqs.question: What does a breeding route show?
faqs.answer: It shows a possible multi-step path from current constraints to a target Pal, including steps, missing Pals, alternatives, and caveats.

faqs.question: Are owned Pals uploaded?
faqs.answer: No. Current copy describes the owned-Pal helper as browser-local localStorage only.

faqs.question: What should I do when no route appears?
faqs.answer: Check names, add owned Pals, increase max generations, relax constraints, and review Data Sources.

blocks.heading: What IVs mean in Palworld
blocks.body: IVs are hidden stat variation values that may explain why two Pals of the same species and level show different HP, Attack, or Defense.

blocks.heading: Inputs needed for an estimate
blocks.body: Ask for Pal, level, observed HP, observed Attack, observed Defense, and any known modifiers the current app supports.

blocks.heading: Why results are ranges
blocks.body: A range means more than one value can explain the observed stats. Rounding, passives, upgrades, condenser stars, formula assumptions, and patch changes can all affect confidence.

blocks.heading: Sample interpretation
blocks.body: If a level 50 Anubis demo returns a broad HP or Attack band, explain it as a planning signal.

blocks.heading: When to use Stats instead
blocks.body: Use IV when you want to work backward from observed stats. Use Stats when you want to preview expected stat bands.

faqs.question: What does the IV Calculator estimate?
faqs.answer: It estimates broad hidden stat ranges from the Pal, level, observed stats, and supported modifier assumptions.

faqs.question: Why is my IV result a range?
faqs.answer: Rounding, missing modifiers, unsupported formulas, or patch changes can make more than one value possible.

faqs.question: How is IV different from Stats?
faqs.answer: IV works backward from observed values; Stats previews expected bands from selected Pal and level.

blocks.heading: Stats Calculator vs IV Calculator
blocks.body: Stats Calculator previews expected HP, Attack, and Defense bands for a Pal and level. IV Calculator estimates hidden stat quality from observed values.

blocks.heading: Expected stat bands
blocks.body: Expected bands help you judge whether a Pal looks close to the current formula assumptions. They are not proof that every modifier has been accounted for.

blocks.heading: How level and base stats affect estimates
blocks.body: Species, level, base stats, supported formulas, and known modifiers shape the returned bands.

blocks.heading: Example interpretation
blocks.body: A level 50 Anubis stat demo can show what a normal comparison looks like.

blocks.heading: Use cases
items: Compare hatch candidates after a breeding project.
Check whether observed stats look unusual before running IV estimates.
Plan a combat or work candidate without treating one stat as the full decision.

faqs.question: What does the Stats Calculator show?
faqs.answer: It previews broad expected HP, Attack, and Defense bands for selected Pal and level inputs.

faqs.question: Should I use Stats before IV?
faqs.answer: Use Stats for broad comparison and IV when you want to estimate hidden stat ranges from observed values.

faqs.question: Where are formula caveats explained?
faqs.answer: Use Data Sources and the IV guide for formula and data-version notes.

blocks.heading: What passive planning can and cannot do
blocks.body: Passive planning helps you organize desired traits by target Pal and role. It does not claim that a selected parent pair or route will produce the desired passive set on the next hatch.

blocks.heading: Choose passives by role
blocks.body: Start from the job. A base worker, combat Pal, mount, utility Pal, and future breeder can need different passive priorities.

table.Planning focus: Work speed, stamina, task fit, and realistic early-game availability.
Damage, survivability, element strategy, and stat review after hatching.
Movement, stamina, travel convenience, and quality-of-life goals.
Traits worth preserving across later projects without promising inheritance outcomes.

blocks.heading: Examples to keep caveated
blocks.body: Use Artisan + Serious as a work-planning example and Swift as a movement/utility example. Recognized passive names are planning targets, not outcome promises.

blocks.heading: Recognized vs unsupported names
blocks.body: If a passive name is unsupported or misspelled, show a clear message and keep the user's plan editable.

blocks.heading: Next step after passive planning
blocks.body: After choosing desired passives, use Breeding for direct parent-pair checks or Route when you need a path from owned Pals.

faqs.question: Can PalCalculator predict passive inheritance odds?
faqs.answer: No. Current copy should not claim exact passive probabilities. Use passive planning as organization, not certainty.

faqs.question: Which passives should I choose first?
faqs.answer: Choose passives by role: work, combat, mount, utility, or future breeder.

faqs.question: Do passives replace IV and stat checks?
faqs.answer: No. Use IV and Stats after hatching candidates when stat quality matters.

blocks.heading: What is different about the 1.0 page
blocks.body: This page is the version-aware entry point for Palworld 1.0 breeding workflows. It can share calculator mechanics with the standard Breeding page while focusing on patch timing, data freshness, and 1.0 caveats.

blocks.heading: Data freshness and patch timing
blocks.body: Palworld 1.0 searches often mean: is this result current enough to use? Show current data version, last-updated date, supported domains, and unsupported domains near the workflow.

blocks.heading: Special-combo coverage caveats
blocks.body: If verified special-combo override table support is pending, say so plainly.

blocks.heading: When to use the standard Breeding Calculator
blocks.body: Use the standard page for general parent-pair education and everyday direct lookups.

blocks.heading: Before relying on an old combo chart
items: Look for normal-formula, special-combo, unavailable, and unsupported labels.
Compare route practicality instead of only checking one pair.
Review Data Sources when another guide disagrees.

faqs.question: What makes this the 1.0 calculator page?
faqs.answer: It foregrounds Palworld 1.0 data-version notes, patch timing, and current supported/unsupported domains.

faqs.question: Is the 1.0 page a duplicate of Breeding Calculator?
faqs.answer: It can share the tool, but the page copy focuses on version freshness and 1.0-specific caveats.

faqs.question: Where can I check data status?
faqs.answer: Use Data Sources for version notes, source categories, unsupported domains, and corrections.
